title: Add quantization profile artifact layout + signed manifest format
author: Quentin Harris
body: Context: As part of the Quantization Profile Library workstream, we need a stable, reviewable, and verifiable on-disk artifact layout for published quantization profiles in the model registry. Runtime workers will fetch profile artifacts by (model, profile_id, version, hardware scope), validate compatibility, and then load the appropriate kernel/calibration sidecars. This PR introduces (1) canonical storage layout conventions under the registry object store and (2) a signed manifest format that acts as the source-of-truth for what constitutes a profile release. Summary of changes: 1) New artifact layout: `quantization-profiles/<publisher>/<model_id>/<profile_id>/<semver>/` with required files `manifest.json` and `manifest.sig`, and optional payloads `calibration/*`, `kernels/*`, `notes.md`, plus `checks/*` for attached validation artifacts. 2) New manifest schema (v1): includes identity fields (model_id, profile_id, version), scope fields (quantization_type, weight_dtype, activation_dtype, kv_cache_dtype, supported_architectures, supported_gpu_families, min_driver, min_cuda), runtime constraints (supported_runtime_versions, required_kernels), integrity fields (sha256 for each payload file), provenance (publisher, created_at, source_commit, build_id), and validation references (perf_report_uri, eval_report_uri, approval). 3) Signing + verification: adds internal library code for manifest signing/verification (ed25519) and enforces that publish API requires a valid signature from an allowed publisher key. Signature covers the canonicalized JSON bytes and includes a key_id in the manifest for auditability. 4) Publish-time validation: server-side checks ensure required files exist, sha256 list matches the uploaded payloads, semver is well-formed, and the directory matches the manifest identity; also prevents overwriting an existing (profile_id, version) unless `--allow-republish` is set (admin only). 5) Backward-compat and forward-compat: manifest includes `schema_version: 1` and allows unknown fields; verification rejects missing required fields but ignores unknown keys so we can extend without breaking older runtimes. Notes: This does not yet wire runtime consumption; it only defines layout + registry-side guarantees. Runtime PRs will rely on `manifest.schema_version`, `files[].sha256`, and `scope` fields for compatibility selection and safe fallback. Test plan: - Unit: manifest canonicalization + signature verify (golden vectors) - Unit: path/identity validation rejects mismatches (e.g., wrong model_id in manifest) - Integration: publish API round-trip with a synthetic profile including calibration + kernel payloads - Security: attempts to upload tampered manifest/payload must fail verification and not become visible to clients Rollout: gated behind `quant_profile_manifest_v1` feature flag in registry publish API; read-path remains unchanged. Checklist: [x] Schema documented and versioned [x] Server-side validation [x] Signature verification + allowed key list plumbing [x] Tests added [x] Migration notes for existing ad-hoc profile uploads (none in prod; only dev buckets) [ ] Follow-up: add `checks/` retention policy + lifecycle rules (separate PR) Related: ENG-18420 (schema + registry storage), ENG-18437 (runtime fetch/cache/compat).
commits: model-registry: add QuantProfileManifest v1 types + canonical JSON encoding
publish: validate profile directory layout + required artifacts
security: implement ed25519 manifest signing/verification + key_id plumbing
api: enforce signed manifest on quantization profile publish (flagged)
tests: add golden vectors and publish integration tests
docs: add artifact layout + manifest field reference
review_conversation: Arjun Desai: Can we add an explicit field for `expected_speedup` / `cost_delta` to the manifest so the library can surface it without scraping notes? (Also: please confirm semver rules: do we allow `-rc` tags for internal preview?)

Quentin Harris: Good call on surfacing speedup/cost deltas, but I’d prefer keeping the manifest strictly about execution + integrity for v1. The library UI can attach perf deltas via `checks/perf_report.json` referenced by URI. For semver: allowing pre-release tags is OK; validator currently accepts full semver including prerelease/build metadata, but publish API defaults to blocking prerelease unless `X-Redwood-Internal: true` header is present. I’ll document this in `manifest_v1.md`.

Hiro Tanaka: `supported_gpu_families` feels underspecified. We need to disambiguate A10 vs A10G, H100 SXM vs PCIe, etc. Can we switch to (vendor, device_id, sm) or at least a normalized GPU SKU string list? Also: where do kernel artifacts live?

Quentin Harris: Updated `scope.supported_gpu_skus` to be a normalized list (e.g., `nvidia-h100-sxm`, `nvidia-l40s`, `nvidia-a10g`) and kept `supported_architectures` for SM-level filtering. Kernel artifacts are now under `kernels/<runtime>/<kernel_pack_id>/...` with hashes tracked in the manifest. Pushed commit `publish: normalize gpu sku list + kernel sublayout`.

Marcus Lin: Two security asks: (1) signature must cover the file hash list as well (not just identity), and (2) key rotation needs an audit trail. How are we storing allowed keys and how does the runtime know what to trust?

Quentin Harris: Signature covers the canonicalized manifest JSON which includes the full file list + sha256; so tampering with hashes/payload mapping breaks verification. Allowed keys are configured server-side in `publisher_keys.yaml` (loaded into memory with periodic refresh); publish endpoint records `publisher_key_id` and `actor` into audit logs. Runtime will trust registry verification and also gets `manifest.sig` to optionally verify client-side later; we’re not requiring runtime verification in v1 but the artifact is there. Added docs section on key rotation + how to revoke a key and block future publishes.

Mateo Alvarez: Nit: we need stable canonicalization rules. Please include a test vector and document exactly what normalization is done (ordering, whitespace, UTF-8). Also can we ensure `created_at` is RFC3339 with timezone?
Quentin Harris: Added canonicalization doc + golden tests (sorted keys, UTF-8, no floats, RFC3339 timestamps enforced). `created_at` now validated as RFC3339 with offset. Thanks.
Priyanka Bose: For publish-time validation, can we allow uploading `notes.md` without hashing it? It’s not executed and will change often.

Quentin Harris: Prefer hashing everything we ship to customers to avoid content tampering, even for notes (it’s still user-facing). Keeping it required if present. We can add `unhashed_files` list later if needed, but I’d rather not create ambiguity in v1.
Arjun Desai: Looks good after the docs update. Approving.
Mateo Alvarez: Approved. Please ensure follow-up for lifecycle rules.
Marcus Lin: Approved with the key rotation doc added.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into `main` by Quentin Harris. Squash commit: `9f2c3a1`.
release_notes: Internal: Model registry now supports a canonical quantization profile artifact layout and signed manifest (schema v1) for publish-time validation and downstream runtime consumption.
